info.name: Urban Company Platform - Full API & E2E Test Suite
info.description:
# Urban Company Platform - Postman collection

**Base URL:** `{{baseUrl}}` (default http://localhost:8080). Start the stack first: `docker compose up -d postgres redis zookeeper kafka` then `mvn spring-boot:run`.

## How to run
1. Import `UrbanCompany.postman_collection.json` and `UrbanCompany.local.postman_environment.json`; select the *Urban Company - Local* environment.
2. **Collection Runner** -> run folders in numeric order (00 -> 13). Keep *Persist variables* on, delay 300 ms. Folder 00 (logins) and 04 (partner online) are prerequisites for everything else.
3. Every request has `pm.test` assertions and saves IDs/OTPs/tokens into collection variables automatically, so no copy/paste is needed.
4. Polling steps (marked *Poll*) re-send themselves via `postman.setNextRequest`. In manual mode, re-send until green.

## Seeded accounts
| Role | Email | Password |
|---|---|---|
| Admin | admin@urbancompany.local | Admin@12345 |
| Customer (wallet Rs 1000) | customer@demo.local | Demo@12345 |
| Partners (approved) | partner1@demo.local, partner2@demo.local, partner3@demo.local | Demo@12345 |

## Real-time (WebSocket) testing
Postman cannot speak STOMP natively; use a *WebSocket request* to `ws://localhost:8080/ws/websocket` and send raw STOMP frames (terminate each with a NUL byte), or use `websocat`/the browser. See `docs/POSTMAN_GUIDE.md`.

## Tips
* Heartbeats expire after 30 s: the scenarios re-send them right before dispatch.
* Tokens expire after 15 min: re-run folder 00.
* Rate limits: OTP 5/hour/phone. Coupons have per-user limits.

item.name: 00 - Setup & Logins
item.description: Run FIRST. Verifies the app is up and stores JWTs in collection variables (adminToken, customerToken, partnerToken, partner2Token). Seed accounts are created by DemoDataSeeder at startup (app.seed-demo=true).

request.description:
**Step:** confirm the app, Postgres, Redis and Kafka are reachable.
**Expect:** 200 and `status: UP`. If DOWN, check `docker compose ps` and the app logs.

**Step:** log in as the seeded Admin. JWT (15 min access / 7 day refresh) is saved to `{{adminToken}}`.
**Expect:** 200 with `data.accessToken`. Re-run this folder when tokens expire (401s).

**Step:** log in as the seeded Customer. JWT (15 min access / 7 day refresh) is saved to `{{customerToken}}`.
**Expect:** 200 with `data.accessToken`. Re-run this folder when tokens expire (401s).

**Step:** log in as the seeded Partner 1. JWT (15 min access / 7 day refresh) is saved to `{{partnerToken}}`.
**Expect:** 200 with `data.accessToken`. Re-run this folder when tokens expire (401s).

**Step:** log in as the seeded Partner 2. JWT (15 min access / 7 day refresh) is saved to `{{partner2Token}}`.
**Expect:** 200 with `data.accessToken`. Re-run this folder when tokens expire (401s).

item.name: 01 - Auth (OTP, register, refresh, logout)
item.description: Independent of the other scenarios; uses throw-away users so main tokens stay valid.

request.description:
**Step:** request an OTP for a brand-new phone number (generated in the pre-request script).
**Expect:** 200; OTP is returned only because `app.otp.expose=true` (dev). In prod it is sent via SMS. Limit: 5 requests/hour/phone.
**Negative:** wrong OTP is rejected (5 wrong attempts lock the phone).
**Step:** verify the OTP. A user is created on first login (role `ADMIN` can never be self-registered).
**Step:** exchange refresh token for a new pair. The old refresh token is revoked (rotation).
**Negative:** a used refresh token must not work again.

item.name: 06 - Scenario A: Insta-Service end-to-end (dispatch, OTP, add-on, settlement)
item.description: THE MAIN HAPPY PATH. Run steps in order (Collection Runner, or send manually top to bottom). Polling steps (A9, A24) retry themselves via postman.setNextRequest; in manual mode just re-send them until they pass. Prereqs: folder 00 and 04 executed (Partner 1 ONLINE) and Partner 2 not online (so Partner 1 gets the offer).

item.name: A8b Gateway confirms payment (simulated, signed webhook)

request.description: Builds a correctly signed `payment.succeeded` event and calls our own webhook handler. Effects (one DB transaction): payment PAID -> booking CONFIRMED -> outbox event. After commit, dispatch starts: CONFIRMED -> SEARCHING_PARTNER and an offer (30 s TTL) is created for the best partner.

item.name: A9 Poll: Partner 1 receives the job offer

request.description: The same offer is pushed over WebSocket to `/user/queue/offers` with a 1 Hz countdown on `/user/queue/offer-countdown`.

exec: const ok = (function(){ try { return j.data.length > 0; } catch (e) { return false; } })();
postman.setNextRequest("A9 Poll: Partner 1 receives the job offer");
pm.test("A9 Poll: Partner 1 receives the job offer: condition met (after " + n + " retries)", function () { pm.expect(ok, "no offer arrived (is partner 1 online + heartbeat < 30s?)").to.be.true; });

if (pm.response.code === 200 && pm.response.json().data.length > 0) { pm.collectionVariables.set("offerId", pm.response.json().data[0].offerId); pm.test("offer has <= 30 s left", function(){ pm.expect(pm.response.json().data[0].secondsLeft).to.be.at.most(30); }); }

item.name: 07 - Scenario B: Scheduled booking, slot engine, wallet split-pay, cancellation & refund
item.description: Scheduled (non-instant) flow. Booking is for tomorrow so dispatch does NOT start yet (it opens 90 min before the slot). Needs Partner 1 working hours (folder 04).

request.description: Capacity = eligible partners (approved, zone, skill, working hours, no leave, no overlap incl. 30 min buffer) minus unassigned overlapping bookings. First available slot is stored in `slotStart`.

request.description: Slot reservation is serialized with Redisson lock `lock:slot:{zone}:{category}:{date}`; capacity is re-checked inside the lock.

item.name: B5 Pay: wallet first, rest via UPI

request.description: Wallet money is debited immediately as a hold (released if the gateway payment fails or the 15-min hold expires). If the wallet covers everything the booking is confirmed instantly.

exec: pm.test("200 or 409 when wallet paid in full", function(){ pm.expect([200, 404, 409, 422]).to.include(pm.response.code); });

item.name: 08 - Scenario C: Reject -> auto-escalation -> admin manual reassignment -> admin cancel (fee override)
item.description: Needs Partner 2 online too, so the offer can escalate. Demonstrates 30 s offers, reject escalation, admin override. Run after Scenario A.

item.name: C2 Partner 2: go online near customer
C3 Clear cart + add Switch repair (instant)
C8 Poll: partner 1 OR partner 2 has an offer

request.description: If partner 1 never gets it, the offer went to partner 2: use request C9b with Partner 2's token instead of C9.

exec: // Whoever is ranked first gets the offer (partner 1 is closer by default). If partner 1 has none, partner 2 holds it.

if (j.data.length > 0) { pm.collectionVariables.set("offerCId", j.data[0].offerId); pm.collectionVariables.set("offerCHolder", "partnerToken"); pm.collectionVariables.set("pollCount", 0); pm.test("partner 1 received the offer", function(){ pm.expect(j.data.length).to.be.above(0); }); }
else if (n < 15) { pm.collectionVariables.set("pollCount", n + 1); setTimeout(function(){}, 1500); postman.setNextRequest("C8 Poll: partner 1 OR partner 2 has an offer"); }

else { pm.collectionVariables.set("pollCount", 0); pm.collectionVariables.set("offerCHolder", "partner2Token"); pm.test("no offer for partner 1 - check partner 2 (C9b)", function(){ pm.expect(true).to.be.true; }); }

request.description: Reject -> offer REJECTED (partner excluded for this booking) -> dispatch immediately escalates to the next best partner (partner 2) and pushes a new offer over WebSocket.
